lines.trans: Report, Mateo! Which room keys got swapped during the noon telephone call?
Look at my paper book: two young hikers with backpacks booked Room Two on the first floor.
Yes, very polite young hikers—and a quiet lady with a hatbox booked Room Six!
Now tell Clara where your glasses were when you handed out keys Two and Six.
Oh dear... on my forehead, and without glasses two and six look almost identical when blurry!
Did the young hikers take the backpacks to Room Six while the hatbox went up to Room Two?!
Lucky for you, boss, both guests dropped their bags outside the doors and went out for lunch!
Really?! Neither guest unlocked the wrong room or unpacked a single shirt yet?
I passed them at the gate two minutes ago asking where to buy noon soup.

words.gloss: ago (hace treinta años = thirty years ago)

And leave two clean notes on each door table explaining the right hook number!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Muy amable is a warm thank-you ('very kind of you').

examples.text: Es una pieza amable.
examples.trans: It is a kind piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: A finger ring or a circular metal fitting.

examples.text: El anillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los anillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Shopping or paper/cloth bag.

examples.text: La bolsa está aquí.
examples.trans: The bag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bolsas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bags from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.text: Abro la cafetería cada mañana.
examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.

examples.text: Cada habitación tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox; la caja also means the cash register/box.

examples.text: La caja está aquí.
examples.trans: The box is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cajas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boxs from the door.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.text: Cambio las toallas cada mañana.
examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.

examples.text: Cambiamos la mesa de sitio.
examples.trans: We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Buttoned shirt.

examples.text: La camisa está aquí.
examples.trans: The shirt is here.

examples.text: Vemos las camisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shirts from the door.

meanings.note: Placed before the word it modifies.

examples.text: Ya son casi las doce.
examples.trans: It is almost twelve o'clock already.

examples.text: Casi olvido la llave en la mesa.
examples.trans: I nearly forgot the key on the table.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Compro pan caliente en la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy warm bread on the corner.

examples.text: Ayer compramos seis limones amarillos.
examples.trans: Yesterday we bought six yellow lemons.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuento).

examples.text: Mi abuela cuenta historias preciosas.
examples.trans: My grandmother tells lovely stories.

examples.text: Conté doce tazas en el armario.
examples.trans: I counted twelve cups in the cupboard.

meanings.note: Opposite of equivocado (wrong).

examples.text: Es una pieza correcta.
examples.trans: It is a right piece.

examples.text: ¡Si hubiera cogido la maleta correcta, ninguno de nosotros estaría aquí esta noche!
examples.trans: If he had picked up the right bag, none of us would be standing here tonight!

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: crucé.

examples.text: Cruzo el puente de piedra cada día.
examples.trans: I cross the stone bridge every day.

examples.text: Cruzamos la plaza hacia el mercado.
examples.trans: We crossed the square toward the market.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.text: Avísame cuando llegue el taxi.
examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

desenfocar.gloss: to throw out of focus, to blur

meanings.en: to throw out of focus, defocus, blur; to lose focus
meanings.note: Regular '-ar' verb (with 'c > qu' spelling change before 'e', e.g., 'desenfoque'); formed from 'des-' + 'enfocar' and used both in camera work and figuratively.

examples.text: No, ¿ves? Eso es desenfocar.
examples.trans: No, see? That's throwing it out of focus.

examples.text: Ten cuidado al mover el objetivo para no desenfocar el primer plano.
examples.trans: Be careful when moving the lens so you don't blur the close-up.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Marks how long an action lasted (durante seis años).

examples.text: Vivió aquí durante seis años.
examples.trans: She lived here for six years.

examples.text: No sonó el teléfono durante la cena.
examples.trans: The phone did not ring during dinner.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: entregué.

examples.text: Entrego el paquete en recepción.
examples.trans: I hand the parcel over at reception.

examples.text: El cartero entregó una carta urgente.
examples.trans: The postman delivered an urgent letter.

meanings.note: La maleta equivocada = the wrong suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza equivocada.
examples.trans: It is a wrong piece.

examples.text: equivocada
examples.trans: wrong

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: expliqué.

examples.text: Te explico el camino en un minuto.
examples.trans: I will explain the way to you in a minute.

examples.text: El arquitecto explicó toda la historia en el patio.
examples.trans: The architect explained the whole story in the courtyard.

frente.gloss: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)

meanings.en: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)
meanings.note: La frente (f) = forehead; frente a frente = face to face.

examples.text: La frente está aquí.
examples.trans: The forehead is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the foreheads from the door.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: Metal hook for shutters, coats, or lanterns.

examples.text: Suelta el gancho de hierro para abrir la ventana.
examples.trans: Unhook the iron hook to open the window.

examples.text: Colgamos el farol grande en el gancho de la pared.
examples.trans: We hung the big lantern on the wall hook.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Plural los huéspedes.

examples.text: El huésped está aquí.
examples.trans: The overnight guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huéspedes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the overnight guests from the door.

meanings.note: Igual que = just like / the same as.

examples.text: Es una pieza igual.
examples.trans: It is a same piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.text: El jefe está aquí.
examples.trans: The boss is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jefes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bosss from the door.

meanings.note: Plural lleva tilde: jóvenes; also used as a noun (el/la joven).

examples.text: Es una pieza joven.
examples.trans: It is a young piece.

examples.text: ¿Voz educada? ¿Joven o mayor?
examples.trans: Polite voice? Young or older?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.text: El libro está aquí.
examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Hacer una llamada = to make a phone call.

examples.text: La llamada está aquí.
examples.trans: The phone call is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llamadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the phone calls from the door.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.text: La llave está aquí.
examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Madre mía! is a mild, warm everyday exclamation across Spain.

examples.text: La madre está aquí.
examples.trans: The mother is here.

examples.text: Vemos las madres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mothers from the door.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Links two simultaneous actions.

examples.text: Espera aquí mientras abro la puerta.
examples.trans: Wait here while I open the door.

examples.text: Preparo el té mientras sale el pan.
examples.trans: I make the tea while the bread comes out.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

examples.text: Primero has dejado la mochila.
examples.trans: First you put down your backpack.

examples.text: Llevo el guion en la mochila.
examples.trans: I carry the script in my backpack.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: El bizcocho está muy rico.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

ninguno.gloss: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)

meanings.en: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)
meanings.note: Shortens to ningún before masculine singular nouns (ningún edificio).

examples.text: Ningún edificio antiguo se derriba aquí.
examples.trans: No historic building is torn down here.

examples.text: Ninguno de los dos se marchó.
examples.trans: Neither of the two walked away.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

meanings.en: gold (precious metal, color, or something of great value)
meanings.note: Masculine noun. Frequently used figuratively in the idiom 'valer oro' ('to be worth its weight in gold / to be priceless'), as when Paquita savors the fresh country air of her hometown.

meanings.en: oros (suit of golden coins in the Spanish card deck)
meanings.note: In the plural ('los oros'), refers to the suit of coins in the traditional Spanish deck of cards ('la baraja española').

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Esa representante tiene un corazón de oro aunque a veces pierda los nervios.
examples.trans: That talent agent has a heart of gold even though she loses her temper sometimes.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg parezco.

examples.text: Este rincón parece un jardín secreto.
examples.trans: This corner looks like a secret garden.

examples.text: La idea nos pareció excelente.
examples.trans: The idea seemed excellent to us.

meanings.note: Used for physical weight or pressure on a key or step.

examples.text: La mesa de roble aguanta mucho peso sin moverse.
examples.trans: The oak table holds plenty of weight without budging.

examples.text: Reparte bien el peso de las cajas al bajarlas.
examples.trans: Balance the weight of the boxes well when carrying them down.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.text: La planta está aquí.
examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Preguntar asks a question; pedir asks for an item or favour.

examples.text: Pregunto en la farmacia por la calle.
examples.trans: I ask at the pharmacy about the street.

examples.text: Una clienta preguntó por el desayuno.
examples.trans: A guest asked about breakfast.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Reservo una mesa tranquila para tres.
examples.trans: I book a quiet table for three.

examples.text: Reservamos la habitación hace un mes.
examples.trans: We booked the room a month ago.

sacar.gloss: to take out; to pull out

meanings.en: to take out; to pull out
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (saqué).

examples.text: Rocío acaba de sacar el pan caliente del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio just took the hot bread out of the oven.

examples.text: Saca las llaves pequeñas del bolsillo del abrigo.
examples.trans: Take the small keys out of your coat pocket.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Masculine singular adjective serio; exceedingly common in the adverbial phrase "en serio" to express disbelief, ask for confirmation, or emphasize sincerity.
Describes a person or organization that is responsible and trustworthy, or a grave situation.

examples.text: ¿En serio te vas? Te lo hace ella, lo hará perfecto.
examples.trans: Are you seriously leaving? She'll do it for you, she'll do it perfectly.

examples.text: ¿En serio? Se va a poner muy contenta. Hasta luego.
examples.trans: Really? She's going to be so happy. See you later.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.text: La señora está aquí.
examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Built from sombra ('shade'), because a brimmed hat casts shade over the face; quitarse el sombrero = to take off one's hat.

examples.text: Un señor mayor con sombrero gris se paró a escuchar en la acera.
examples.trans: An older gentleman in a grey hat stopped to listen on the pavement.

examples.text: Se quitó el sombrero con respeto al entrar en la sala.
examples.trans: He took off his hat respectfully as he stepped into the room.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.text: La sopa está aquí.
examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Pura suerte = sheer luck.

examples.text: La suerte es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The luck is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la suerte.
examples.trans: We talk about the luck.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.text: Sí, la habitación está lista.
examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.

examples.text: ¡Claro que sí, pase usted!
examples.trans: Of course, come right in!

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.text: El café todavía está caliente.
examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Todavía no son las doce.
examples.trans: It is not twelve o'clock yet.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Accented subject pronoun (tú mismo = you yourself).

examples.text: Tú conoces muy bien el barrio.
examples.trans: You know the neighbourhood very well.

examples.text: Pruébalo tú mismo.
examples.trans: Try it yourself.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

valer.gloss: to be worth; to cost; to work / count

meanings.en: to be worth; to cost; to work / count
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg valgo.

examples.text: Cada minuto de calma vale oro.
examples.trans: Every minute of peace is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: ¿Vale este billete para el tren regional?
examples.trans: Is this ticket valid for the regional train?

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.

examples.text: Soy yo, abre por favor.
examples.trans: It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Accented él ('he/him') is distinct from unaccented article el ('the').

examples.text: Él trabaja en el ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: He works at City Hall.

examples.text: Sube a hablar con él un minuto.
examples.trans: Go upstairs and talk to him for a minute.
